comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C34-C37. Both evaluations find the hyperoxia model produces alveolar simplification with emphysematous changes, supported by histological and physiological data. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C39-C43 regarding epithelial TGF-β signaling protection. Both evaluations support the findings and acknowledge the protective role. OpenEval includes C38 while peer review does not, but both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on claims C44-C47. Both evaluations affirm the reduction in PDGFR-α+ cells shown by flow cytometry and consistency with prior studies. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on scRNA-seq findings (C48-C50). Peer review additionally includes C4 and emphasizes validation with external datasets. Both praise the comprehensive single-cell approach and rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial agreement on pathway analysis. OpenEval focuses on IPA analysis (C51-C52, C5) while peer review emphasizes NicheNet analysis (C5, C51-C56). Both accept the pathway findings as valid mechanistic insights and rate as SUPPORTED.

Overlap on NicheNet predictions (C53-C56). OpenEval notes computational predictions require experimental validation while peer review praises the analytical approach. Both rate as SUPPORTED but OpenEval is more cautious about causal claims.

Strong agreement on TGF-β inhibition worsening disease (C57-C60, C6-C8). Both evaluations emphasize this surprising finding contradicts initial hypotheses but is well-supported. OpenEval includes C61 while peer review does not. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial agreement on genetic validation. OpenEval focuses on Cre driver validation (C62-C63) while peer review emphasizes mesenchymal TGF-β receptor deletion (C62-C67). Both rate as SUPPORTED and note robustness of genetic approaches.
Strong agreement on mesenchymal TGF-β receptor deletion (C64-C67). Both evaluations accept these findings as robust evidence supporting protective role of TGF-β. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial agreement on integrin findings. OpenEval focuses on negative αvβ6 result (C69-C70, C75) while peer review covers broader integrin findings (C69-C76). Both accept the systematic approach to identifying TGF-β activators and rate as SUPPORTED.
Strong agreement on mesenchymal αv-integrin role (C72-C74, C76). Both evaluations accept these findings as identifying key TGF-β activators. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on proliferation defects (C77-C81, C9). Both evaluations strongly support these findings as key mechanistic contributions, with temporal analysis showing proliferation defects precede cell loss. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on proliferation defects across models (C82-C85). Both evaluations accept consistency across models as strong evidence. OpenEval notes C85 is speculative requiring validation, while peer review treats generalizability as established. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on Ect2 sufficiency experiment (C86-C93, C10, C100). Both evaluations treat this as a major finding demonstrating sufficiency of impaired proliferation. Peer review additionally includes C103. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Minimal overlap on C88-C89. OpenEval focuses on flow cytometry validation across injury models while peer review groups C88 with methodological claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on overarching conclusions (C94-C95). Both evaluations accept TGF-β as compensatory rather than pathologic based on comprehensive experimental evidence. Peer review additionally includes C101-C102. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial agreement on background claims. OpenEval groups C1-C2, C11-C19, C96 as clinical context while peer review includes broader background (C1-C32, C96-C97). Both rate as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Strong agreement on scientific background (C3, C20-C33). Both evaluations accept these as well-established context. OpenEval notes C33 acknowledges controversy while peer review addresses this separately. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluation of C33 controversy. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting appropriate acknowledgment of controversy, while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, indicating spatial validation would strengthen conclusions about myofibroblast loss.
Minimal overlap on background claims (C61, C68, C71, C97, C98). OpenEval groups these as contextual citations while peer review includes C98 with methodological claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Partial agreement on summary inferences. OpenEval groups C99, C101-C103 as integrative conclusions while peer review includes C101-C102 with main conclusions about TGF-β role. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Minimal overlap on C99. OpenEval treats as summary inference supported by EdU data while peer review groups with methodological claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
